content.comment_body: Hi [user_name], I followed the copy and paste instructions you gave, but now when I try to simulate, I get a message saying there are contacts that are not connected. If I select "Yes," an error occurs. However, when converting to FBD, it says: "Maximum nesting depth: An unconnected input connector is converted to a low input signal." When I return to my ladder program and use Ctrl + G (Go to Block), I see inputs in my program that don't actually exist and cannot be deleted. Is there something I can do to resolve this issue? Thanks

I managed to fix the issue, although maybe not in the correct way, but it works. I copied my entire program, making sure not to include the connection to the power bus. To do this, I zoomed out to 25%, used the mouse wheel to select all contacts, connectors, timers, and other elements, and then pasted everything into a new Ladder Diagram. After pressing F3 to simulate, a message asks if I want to "Connect the contacts to the power bus?" Selecting "Yes," the software connects all my networks to the power bus automatically. Now, the new program contains only inputs and outputs that actually exist.

This seems like a bug in [product_name] [version_no] for LAD mode. If you select a line connected to the bus and move it up or down, it loses connection to the bus. The workaround is to disconnect and delete every line connected to the power bus, then reconnect them. Hopefully, this will be fixed in future versions! Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users have experienced issues in the Ladder Diagram simulation process with [product_name] [version_no], specifically after using copy and paste, which leads to error messages about unconnected contacts and non-existent inputs that cannot be deleted. The common solution is to rebuild the program without copying power bus connections and rely on the software to reconnect them automatically. Another user notices this is likely a software bug related to moving bus-connected lines, which breaks the connection.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable copy-and-paste functionality where connections are maintained, and it is straightforward to identify and remove redundant or non-existent ladder diagram elements.
